workflow: Collect the minimum source records needed to evaluate craft brewery batch costing and SKU profitability.
Normalize revenue, cost, volume, timing, and exception inputs before calculation.
Calculate the margin result and expose the assumptions behind it.
Let the owner, head brewer, or finance manager approve an action and compare the eventual result with the forecast.
fields: source record and reporting period
customer, job, asset, location, or contract identifier
revenue or avoided-loss amount
variable cost and allocated capacity cost
volume, timing, utilization, or risk inputs
recommended action, owner, confidence, and review date
mistakes: Treating revenue as profit while omitting variable and capacity costs.
Automating a recommendation before source data and assumptions are reviewable.
Using one threshold for unlike customers, jobs, assets, or seasons.
Measuring recommendations without recording the action and eventual outcome.

metrics.name: incremental gross profit or avoided loss
metrics.formula: realized revenue plus avoided loss minus variable and capacity cost
metrics.decision: keep only actions that create a positive realized contribution

metrics.name: financial realization rate
metrics.formula: realized financial result divided by the approved expected result
metrics.decision: find recommendations whose promised value does not survive execution

metrics.name: forecast error
metrics.formula: absolute expected-versus-realized difference divided by the realized result
metrics.decision: recalibrate assumptions or separate unlike cases

metrics.name: decision cycle time
metrics.formula: approved-action timestamp minus qualifying-trigger timestamp
metrics.decision: remove delays that cause an otherwise valuable opportunity to expire

alternatives.name: Owner-maintained spreadsheet
alternatives.best: volume is low, one person owns the decision, and assumptions change often
alternatives.limit: manual joins and inconsistent follow-through become hard to audit

alternatives.name: Existing industry-system reports
alternatives.best: the source system already contains costs, outcomes, and decision rules
alternatives.limit: reports often stop at activity or revenue instead of the full money outcome

alternatives.name: General BI tool or analyst
alternatives.best: the buyer has data skills and needs several adjacent analyses
alternatives.limit: analysis alone may not put an approved action back into the operating cycle

triggers: a new quote, order, job, customer, asset, or contract
a material change in cost, price, utilization, or timing
a renewal, repricing, planning, or exception-review cycle
examples: a high-revenue case that becomes unattractive after variable costs
an underused capacity slot where a targeted action creates incremental margin
an exception whose missing evidence would otherwise hide revenue or increase risk
rules: Never recommend an action when required source inputs are missing or stale.
Show the financial formula and assumptions beside every recommendation.
Require human approval for customer-facing price, contract, or schedule changes.
Recalculate after the realized outcome so future recommendations can improve.
